hypotheses.title: Short-Horizon Volume-Weighted Price Reversal
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Institutional liquidity shocks cause transient price overshoot over 1-to-5 day horizons. When price deviates sharply from VWAP or rolling averages accompanied by abnormal volume, liquidity replenishment by market makers causes predictable mean-reversion within subindustries.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Signal produces negative Sharpe when holding horizon is extended past 10 days, or when subindustry neutralization is removed.

candidates.rationale: Daily close-to-VWAP divergence normalized within subindustry
3-day price momentum weighted by abnormal volume surge relative to 20-day average
Rolling z-score of price relative to 10-day mean, smoothed over a 5-day window
